emergency.notes: 911 serves all emergencies nationwide. In remote areas, satellite communicators are recommended as cell coverage is limited. Non-emergency police: dial the local police station number.

travelAdvisory.summary: Exercise normal precautions in Canada. Canada is a stable, safe country for visitors with a high standard of living and a well-functioning rule of law.

travelAdvisoryUK.summary: Most visits to Canada are trouble-free. Be prepared for extreme weather conditions, particularly in winter and in wildfire season.

healthcare.systemType: Universal public (for residents); private for tourists
healthcare.costForTourists: Tourists do not have access to the public healthcare system and pay full rates. Walk-in clinic: $150-300. Emergency room: $1,000-3,000+. Hospital stay: $2,000-5,000+/night. Healthcare is world-class but very expensive without insurance.
healthcare.pharmacyAccess: Pharmacies (Shoppers Drug Mart, Rexall, London Drugs) are widespread. Many OTC medications available. Pharmacists speak English and French.
healthcare.hospitalNotes: Major cities have excellent university hospitals and trauma centers. Rural and remote areas have very limited facilities — medevac may be required. Wait times at public emergency rooms can be long (4-8+ hours for non-critical cases).
vaccinationsRecommended: Rabies (if spending time outdoors in rural areas)
healthcare.insuranceAdvice: Travel insurance is essential for tourists. Healthcare costs without insurance are among the highest in the world. Ensure your policy covers emergency evacuation, as remote areas may require helicopter transport.

pharmacy.hours: Most pharmacies open 9am-9pm; 24-hour pharmacies available in major cities; pharmacy chains include Shoppers Drug Mart, Rexall, and London Drugs
pharmacy.tips: Pharmacists are highly trained and helpful. You may need a prescription for medications that are over-the-counter in the US. Bring a doctor's note for any controlled medications. Minor ailments can be treated by pharmacists under Canada's minor ailment prescribing program in many provinces.

vaccinations.notes: No required vaccinations for entry. Ensure routine vaccinations are up to date. No special vaccines needed for most travelers.

water.notes: Tap water is safe to drink throughout Canada. Bottled water is widely available. In remote northern areas, follow local advisories.

healthcare.foodSafetyTips: Canada has excellent food safety standards. All food sold commercially is safe. Be cautious with wild game or fish caught in areas with environmental advisories. Street food in cities is generally safe.

travelInsurance.tips: Canada's healthcare is expensive for tourists (hospital stays can cost $3,000-$5,000+/day). Travel insurance with medical coverage is strongly recommended. Some provinces may provide emergency care to foreign nationals at full cost. Consider coverage that includes medical evacuation to the US if needed.

healthcare.qualityNotes: World-class healthcare system. Wait times can be long for non-emergency care even for residents. Tourists are charged for all services. Pharmacies widely available with English-speaking staff.

medications.generalAdvice: Canada allows travelers to bring personal-use quantities of prescription medications (generally up to 90 days' supply) in original labeled containers. All controlled substances must be declared to the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA). Carry a doctor's letter and original prescription for all medications, especially controlled substances.

controlledSubstances.note: Despite cannabis being legal in Canada, it is ILLEGAL to bring cannabis across the Canadian border in either direction. This includes all forms — flower, edibles, oils, CBD. Do not attempt to import or export cannabis.
Controlled under Canada's Controlled Drugs and Substances Act. Carry original prescription, doctor's letter, and keep in labeled container. Declare at customs.
Schedule III controlled substances. Carry in original prescription container with your name on the label. Bring a doctor's letter. Quantities should match your stay duration.
Schedule IV controlled substances. Keep in original prescription container with documentation.
Available behind the pharmacy counter in limited quantities. Requires ID and pharmacist consultation. Tracked due to precursor chemical concerns.
Schedule III substances. Illegal to possess or import despite some therapeutic exemptions granted to specific practitioners.

scams.name: Airport taxi overcharging
scams.description: Unlicensed or unofficial taxi drivers at airports quote flat rates far above metered fares, especially targeting new arrivals unfamiliar with local prices.
scams.avoidance: Use only official taxi queues or rideshare apps (Uber, Lyft) at airports. Toronto Pearson has fixed-rate taxis to downtown (~$55-65 CAD).

scams.name: Timeshare / vacation club scams
scams.description: Tourists in resort areas are invited to 'free gift' presentations that turn into high-pressure timeshare sales lasting hours.
scams.avoidance: Decline all offers of free gifts contingent on attending a presentation. These are never good deals.

scams.name: Online vacation rental scams
scams.description: Fraudulent listings on rental sites offer cottages, cabins, or condos at attractive prices. Payments are taken but keys are never provided.
scams.avoidance: Use established platforms with verified reviews. Pay via credit card for chargeback protection. Never wire money directly to a landlord.

connectivity.simOptions: Tourist SIM cards from Rogers, Bell, or TELUS at airports and phone stores. 30-day tourist packages: ~CAD $35-60 for 15-50GB. eSIM via Airalo. Freedom Mobile offers cheaper rates for tourists staying in cities.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Free WiFi at airports, coffee shops (Tim Hortons, Starbucks), malls, and libraries. Hotel WiFi is standard. Rural areas have very limited connectivity.
connectivity.bestOption: Prepaid SIM from TELUS or Rogers (best national coverage including rural areas). eSIM if your phone supports it. Activate before leaving the airport.

cultural.tipping: Tipping is standard and expected. Restaurants: 15-20% on the pre-tax amount. Taxis: 10-15%. Hotel porters: CAD $2-3 per bag. Hairdressers: 15-20%. Automatic gratuity may be added for groups of 6+.
cultural.dressCode: Casual and practical. Layer up in winter. Smart casual for restaurants. No strict dress codes except at very formal events.
cultural.greetings: Handshake is standard for formal meetings. Hugs or kisses on the cheek among friends. 'How are you?' is a greeting, not a genuine inquiry — 'Fine, thanks' is the expected response.
taboos: Confusing Canadians with Americans — they are proud of the distinction
Being impolite or aggressive in public — Canadians are famously courteous
Not saying please and thank you
Being overly loud in residential areas
cultural.haggling: Not practiced in stores, restaurants, or services. Negotiation is possible when buying from private sellers or at some antique markets.

phrases.local: I don't understand / Je ne comprends pas

safety.lgbtSafety: Excellent. Canada is one of the most LGBTQ+-inclusive countries in the world. Same-sex marriage has been legal since 2005. Toronto and Vancouver have vibrant LGBTQ+ communities. Pride events are major celebrations.
safety.soloFemaleSafety: Very safe. Canada ranks highly for gender equality. Exercise normal urban precautions at night. Remote areas require practical safety planning.
safety.notes: Canada is one of the safest countries in the world. Main concerns for tourists are weather extremes (blizzards, wildfires, extreme cold), wildlife encounters in national parks, and petty theft in major cities. Always check current wildfire and weather alerts before venturing into wilderness areas.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: no visa required (but passport required since 2009). UK, EU, Australia: eTA required ($7 CAD) for air travel. Visa-free or eTA for 60+ countries.
practical.timeZone: UTC-3:30 (Newfoundland) to UTC-8:00 (Pacific) — spans 6 time zones
practical.bestTimeToVisit: June-August for warm weather and outdoor activities. December-March for skiing. September-October for fall foliage. Avoid January-February in central Canada (extreme cold, -30 to -40°C possible).

immediate: Evacuate immediately when an evacuation order is issued — do not wait
Take your go-bag (medications, documents, phone charger, 3-day supplies)
Close all windows, doors, and vents to slow smoke infiltration
Follow designated evacuation routes — do not use unauthorized roads
Notify your contacts of your evacuation destination
Wear N95 mask when in smoky air
after: Do not return to evacuated areas until authorities give the all-clear
Check air quality index (AQHI) at www.airhealth.ca before outdoor activity
Inspect your property for structural damage and hot spots before re-entering

immediate: Stay indoors if conditions are extreme
If driving, keep an emergency kit in your vehicle (blanket, shovel, sand/salt, water, snacks)
Do not leave your vehicle if stranded — it is easier to find
Dress in layers — frostbite can occur in minutes in extreme wind chill
after: Clear snow from roof if heavy accumulation (risk of collapse)
Watch for ice on roads and sidewalks

Apply for emergency travel document or replacement passport
Keep copies of all documents filed
Go to nearest police station for official report
Request a copy of the report in English if possible
Keep report number for insurance claims
Move to a safe location if possible
Contact your rental company if applicable
Have your location ready to share
